title: Customer opt-in subprocessor controls + archival window SKUs experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Large enterprise buyers increasingly request fine-grained control over which subprocessors can process their EU/UK traffic and want predictable retention windows for model cache and logs. Current Redwood packaging bundles residency and retention into coarse SKUs that force legal negotiation or custom contracts. Goal: Run a product-led experiment to surface a self-serve opt-in flow for subprocessor visibility/attestation plus an optional paid 'archival window' SKU that extends retention for model cache and request logs. We will measure commercial uplift, legal friction reduction, and incremental operational cost.
acceptance_criteria: A self-serve checkbox flow exists in the contract/config console where customers can opt into: (1) standard subprocessors, (2) EU-only allowed subprocessors, (3) attestation-required subprocessors.
A new billing SKU called 'Archival Window' is available with 30/90/365 day options; selecting it updates price and creates correct invoicing line items.
Backend enforcement: retention TTLs and optional encryption-at-rest scope respect the selected archival window without elevating latency above SLOs.
Legal/Privacy: standard contract addendum template for attested subprocessors is generated and approved by legal.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Feb 2025): Legal drafts addendum and attestation template; engineering scoping and perf estimate.
Phase 1 (Mar 2025): Internal beta with 3 pilot customers; manual contract sign-off but self-serve config in console.
Phase 2 (Apr 2025): Public opt-in in console; billing SKU enabled; telemetry & billing validation.
Phase 3 (May 2025): Iterate on pricing bands and automate attestation workflows; incorporate learnings into docs and sales playbook.
metrics: Conversion: % of trial/orgs that enable attestation or archival SKU within 30 days of signup (target +6% vs baseline)
ARR impact: additional MRR attributable to Archival Window SKU (target $40k MRR from pilot cohort)
Legal overhead: # of manual redlines / customer negotiations reduced compared to baseline (target -30%)
Ops cost delta: incremental storage and retrieval cost per 1k requests for 30/90/365 day SKUs
Support load: # of privacy-related tickets opened during pilot (goal <= 15 tickets per pilot customer)
Latency/SLO: 95th percentile token latency change after archival enablement (target <5% regression)
Escalations: number of sign-offs required from Legal/Privacy per customer (target decrease)
decisions: Offer three archival windows (30, 90, 365 days) priced as relative multipliers: 1.0x / 1.6x / 2.8x baseline storage unit costs + 10% ops premium.
Subprocessor options presented as opt-in tiers: 'Standard (default)', 'EU-only', 'Attested'. Attested tier requires a signed addendum and pushes attestation certificate into customer portal.
We will not restrict model catalog by default; instead routing policy will allow customers to request EU-only routing for eligible models and receive fallback explanations.
Implementation will use existing retention TTLs and metadata flags; no new datastore introduced to minimize engineering work.

risks_mitigation: Risk: Sales ask for custom subprocessors list outside of the opt-in tiers. Mitigation: Add 'custom negotiation' flag requiring Legal review and route to enterprise contracting path.
Risk: Extended retention increases attack surface. Mitigation: Mandatory customer opt-in and explicit encryption scope in addendum; Security to validate HSM/KMS usage.
Risk: Billing disputes on archival charges. Mitigation: Show preview of invoice lines in console before purchase and generate signed quote for pilot customers.
notes: Follow-up: Schedule a cross-functional demo with Sales/Support to walk the pilot flow and FAQ (owner: Aisha).
Customer ask: One pilot requested export of the exact subprocessors list as CSV; product to evaluate feasibility for Phase 1.
If pilot shows >10% MRR uplift from archival SKU, prepare a roadmap item to expand to dedicated/reserved capacity customers with different pricing multipliers.
